title: Technological Advancements in the Tunability and Applications of Electrically Driven Ultrafast Electron Microscopy
content: Recent advancements have pushed electrically driven ultrafast electron microscopy (UEM) into an application space which was previously difficult for any technique to achieve. As most ultrafast techniques, electrically driven UEM systems rely on stroboscopic imaging based on a pulsed probe and periodic pump synchronized at the exact same frequency. To date, electrically driven UEM systems operate by a voltage-based pump, probe or both. At BNL, we use an entirely electrically driven system which can combine different electrical signals (AC, RF, pulsed DC) to enable the elucidation of materials dynamics as long as frequency matching is achieved [1, 2]. Our system can generate electron pulses between 1 picosecond and 2.2 nanoseconds at frequencies ranging from 1 Hz to 12 GHz. Currently, the system is not completely fluid within this parameter space, because a myriad of equipment is needed to achieve the tunability, but the advancements of just a few years is monumental. Additionally, electrically driven systems contain two key advantages in terms of application driven research alone. First, sample preparation is in the form of real-world devices complete with electrical connections and custom chip creation. Second, electronic signal generators have significant control over the shape of the excitation on the sample, including square, sine or custom signals. With these two advantages, in operando microscopy has taken a huge leap forward into the time-resolved domain by enabling the elucidation of device dynamics.
